title.narrative: Regional Trade for Development-economic cooperation for Australia’s Free Trade Agreements with ASEAN

description.narrative: The Regional Trade for Development (RT4D) investment responds to ASEAN’s priorities for trade policy capacity building and economic cooperation to implement and maximise the benefits of the ASEAN-Australia-New Zealand FTA (AANZFTA) and the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) Agreement. RT4D mainstreams Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) principles into its activities and collaborates with the Trade and Gender Equality Incubator (TGEI) to further research and pilot initiatives that advance gender equality within trade.

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

description.narrative: The Regional Trade for Development (RT4D) initiative assists ASEAN Member States (AMS), to realise the full benefits of the ASEAN-centered free trade agreements. The Upgraded AANZFTA will allow exporters to benefit from full cumulation under Rules of Origin. To help AMS implement this provision, RT4D conducted a gap analysis and technical workshop in November 2023. A majority of workshop participants (98%) stated that the workshop significantly improved their understanding of the provisions and 50% of participants said that they are likely to apply the knowledge they learned from the workshop to implement FTAs within their area of competence.

Through RT4D, Australia supports ASEAN to realise the benefits of AANZFTA and RCEP. RT4D partnered with Cambodia’s Ministry of Commerce to deliver the “Enhancing the Private Sector’s Understanding and Utilisation of RCEP Benefits” project between November 2024 and February 2025. ‍ RT4D delivered a one-day workshop attended by 151 participants, including six organisations of people with disabilities (OPDs) and three people with disability (PWDs). This supported disability equity by: ‍ -Prioritising inclusion of OPDs and PWDs in participant selection, including covering participation costs and utilising accessible venues ‍ -Prioritising OPDs and PWDs as speakers, including a PWD who led an OPD to provide vocational training to PWDs to develop and sell products internationally ‍ -Facilitating discussions between OPDs and PWDs and policymakers (30 per cent of participants) on the obstacles that they face in utilising RCEP, and ‍ -Providing capacity building to OPDs and PWDs, building their knowledge to better take advantage of RCEP. ‍ The project resulted in 98.5 per cent of participants reporting improved ability to utilise RCEP. RT4D contributed to disability equity by building the capabilities and capacities of OPDs and PWDs, supporting their growth and integration into regional and global value chains, ensuring that OPDs and PWDs can also benefit from RCEP.

Through RT4D, Australia supports ASEAN to realise the benefits of their two regional free trade agreements – AANZFTA and RCEP. RT4D supported Lao PDR’s Department of Intellectual Property, Ministry of Industry and Commerce to deliver the ‘Accelerating Women's Advancement in Intellectual Property (IP)’ project between November 2023 and November 2024. ‍ The project included four activities that equipped women-owned micro, small and medium sized enterprises (MSMEs) to better use IP to increase the value of their products. The project targeted products certified under the One District One Product Program – an initiative to open export markets for locally made goods. ‍ RT4D successfully supported 60 participants, including 46 government officials and 14 MSMEs (all women-owned), across four activities comprising two trademark development assistance workshops, mentorship support and a product showcase during the 2024 IP Week. ‍ The project resulted in all 14 women-owned MSMEs successfully developing and registering trademark designs and showcasing their newly trademarked products at the 2024 IP Week in Lao PDR. RT4D contributed to women’s economic empowerment by strengthening the protection and market recognition of these MSMEs, allowing them to distinguish themselves and position their products for domestic and international markets, ensuring that women can benefit from AANZFTA and RCEP.

Through the Regional Trade for Development (RT4D) initiative, Australia supports the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) to realise the benefits offered by the Agreement Establishing the ASEAN-Australia-New Zealand Free Trade Area (AANZFTA) and the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP). RT4D worked with the AANZFTA Trade in Goods Committee to deliver the “Addressing Obstacles to Monitoring Utilisation of AANZFTA Tariff Preferences” project between May 2024 and June 2025. ‍ The project designed a regional mechanism to monitor business utilisation of AANZFTA, which included delivery of: ‍ -a background paper documenting AANZFTA Parties’ existing experiences, capabilities and challenges; ‍ -two regional workshops (60 government officials) to agree on the mechanism’s requirements; and ‍ -a policy paper outlining the agreed mechanism and implementation workplan. ‍ The project resulted in an approved mechanism (to be piloted in 2026 and launched in 2027), with 93.6% participants reporting improved understanding of the benefits and process to monitor utilisation and 87.2% participants reporting they would apply learnings to their work in monitoring AANZFTA. ‍ ‍ RT4D contributed to greater participation in rules-based trade by building the capacity of AANZFTA government officials to assess how businesses benefit and utilise AANZFTA, strengthening their capacity to ensure AANZFTA remains responsive to private sector needs.
